 Order

1. By way of the present criminal revision petition, the revisionist has impugned the order dated 01.07.2024 (herein after referred to as impugned order), passed by the Court of Ms. Rajat Goel,
learned CJM, South West, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi in FIR no. 55/2022, PS EOW, titled 'State vs.
Mukesh Kumar Singh', whereby the respondent no. 2 has been permitted custody parole for execution and registration of SPA in respect of Sale of his property situated at A-603, Ircon Apartments, Plot no. 14, Dwarka, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as the property).
2. Notice of the revision petition was served upon the respondent No.1/State on whose behalf the same was accepted by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor on 04.07.2024.

Notice was also Eminent Officers Welfare Society vs State And Ors on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49305278/
1 served upon the respondent No. 2, who entered appearance on 06.07.2024 and contested the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. During arguments, Mr. Varun Singh, learned counsel for the revisionist has submitted that the order passed by the learned Trial Court is erroneous and is not based upon the proper appreciation of the facts and the law.

That the present FIR was got registered against the accused/respondent no.
2 on allegations that he in conspiracy with other co-accused had cheated the complainant society and its 120 members by siphoning off cash totaling more than Rs.20 crores.

He has further argued that the said order was passed without notice to the revisionist which is in violation of the dictum in Jagjeet Singh and Others v. Ashish Mehra @ Monu and Ors., (2022) 3 SCC Criminal 560 , wherein it was held that the complainant has every right to participate at every stage of the proceedings.

entities.text: Jagjeet Singh and Others v. Ashish Mehra @ Monu and Ors., (2022) 3 SCC Criminal 560
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is argued that there are assertions in the charge-sheet that accused had purchased flat bearing no.
A-603, Ircon Apartment, Sector-18, Dwarka, Delhi and one Tata Hexa Car from the money received from the complainant society.
That there are specific allegations in the charge-sheet that the funds of the complainant were diverted and siphoned by the accused and were used to purchase the said property.

That the complainant had moved an application U/s 451 Cr.P.C. seeking directions from the Court to hand over physical possession or in alternate award the proceeds out of the sale of the said property which was dismissed by the Ld. Trial Court vide order dated 30.04.2024.

That it was observed in the said order that the issue whether the said properties were purchased out of proceeds of crime is a matter of trial and could not be determined at that stage merely because the IO had opined so.
That it was also observed that allowing the application of the complainant/revisionist herein would tantamount to adjudging the accused persons guilty before conclusion of trial.

That,
however, the learned Trial Court permitted the accused/applicant to execute and register his SPA while observing that the accused has every right to deal with his property as any other person.
That the impugned order is thus not an interlocutory order.

Reliance is placed on the pronouncements in Ram Kishore Thakur vs. Shyam Bihari Giri, 1991 SCC Online Pat 8; Directorate of Enforcement through Assistant Director vs. Dr. Vinod Bhandari and Ors., 2023 SCC Online MP 4114; Ganesha Murthy vs. State, Crl. R.C. No. 1369 of 2018 decided on 17.12.2018.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Assistant Director vs. Dr. Vinod Bhandari and Ors., 2023 SCC Online MP 4114
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Ld. Addl. PP for the State has argued that there are allegations in the charge-sheet that the property was purchased by diverting funds of the complainant.

That order dated 01.07.2024 contains observations that the said property is of the accused but does not contain any finding whether it was purchased from tainted money or not but is rather based on the finding that the property is of the accused.
That the order is thus not interlocutory.

It is further submitted that the property as per assertions in the charge-sheet was purchased from tainted money and the money trail has been mentioned in the charge-sheet itself.
5.
It is argued on behalf of respondent no. 2 that the property in question was never seized or attached.
That the IO merely issued notice to the concerned bank not to hand over documents of the property without permission of the court.

That thereafter, the respondent made application before the Hon'ble Court and repaid the loan amount and the title documents were released to the accused/applicant by permission of the Ld. Trial court.
That application of the revisionist U/s 451 Cr.P.C. seeking possession of the property or in the alterative sale proceeds of the said property was already dismissed by the Ld. Trial Court.

That the said property is of the respondent and his wife Eminent Officers Welfare Society vs State And Ors on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49305278/
2 and they have every right to deal with it as per law.

entities.text: Eminent Officers Welfare Society vs State And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That the present revision petition is not maintainable as the order dated 01.07.2024 merely granted custody parole to respondent no. 2.
That the said order was interlocutory order and the present revision petition is liable to be dismissed on this short ground.
That the judgments relied upon by the revisionist are not applicable to the facts of the present case and were passed in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the said cases.
It is argued that the revision petition may be dismissed.
6. The revision petition as well as the trial court record have been carefully and thoroughly perused.

The respective submissions of learned counsel for revisionist, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1/State as well as learned counsel for the respondent No.2 have been duly considered.
7.
Before proceeding any further it would be appropriate to refer to the brief facts of the case culminating into the present adjudication.
Briefly stated, the respondent no. 2 has been charge-sheeted for commission of offence U/s 409/420/406/424/411/120 B IPC.
The respondent no. 2 is stated to be the Director of M/s Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd.

entities.text: Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per allegations in the charge-sheet, the said company, which was a defunct company entered into an MoU with the complainant society to get land registered in its name.

The charge-sheet mentions that the Directors of M/s Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd. had no intention to procure land for the society since inception and they were siphoning off the money for their personal use and monetary gains.

entities.text: Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: There are specific allegations against the respondent no. 2 that he received money from the complainant society and siphoned the funds with the help of M/s Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd.

entities.text: Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: There are further allegations against respondent no. 2 that he was authorized signatory in all bank accounts of M/s Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd. and the money received from the society was transferred into his personal accounts which was further misappropriated by him.

entities.text: Khushi Properties and Developers Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: There are assertions in the charge-sheet that the respondent no. 2 purchased inter alia a flat no. A-603, Ircon Apartment, Sector-18, Dwarka, Delhi and transactions of his bank account reveal that money obtained from the society was paid against this flat.

That transfer pattern of bank accounts of respondent no. 2 shows that he received Rs.16.28 crores from the society in 39 transactions and he kept diverting the money over a period of four years and misappropriated the same for his personal gains.

8. The very first objection of Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 2 is that the impugned order dated 01.07.2024 is interlocutory order and the present revision petition is not maintainable on this short ground.

Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the revisionist has placed reliance upon pronouncements in Ram Kishore, Directorate of Enforcement and Ganesha Murthy (supra) to contend that the impugned order is not interlocutory order.
9. It would be appropriate here to refer to the settled proposition of law on the point.
It is well settled having been held in a catena of judicial pronouncements that any order, which substantially affects rights of the parties, can not be called an interlocutory order.

The ratio in R.P. Kapoor v.
State of Punjab, AIR 1960 SC 866 : 1960 Cri LJ 1239 : Amar Nath v. State of Harayana, AIR 1977 SC 2185: (1977 Cri LJ 1891), Madhu Limaye v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1978 SC 47 : 1978 Cri LJ 165 and V.C. Shukla v. State through CBI, AIR 1980 SC 962 :
Eminent Officers Welfare Society vs State And Ors on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49305278/
3 (1980 Cri LJ 690), can fruitfully be adverted to on this aspect.

R.P. Kapoor v.
State of Punjab, AIR 1960 SC 866 : 1960 Cri LJ 1239
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of Amar Nath, (1977 Cri LJ 1891) (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court had made the following pertinent observations :
(Para 6) "It seems to us that the term "interlocutory order in Section 397(2) of the 1973 Code has- been used in a restricted sense and not in any broad or artistic sense.
It merely denotes orders of a purely interim or temporary nature which do not decide or bouch the important rights or the liabilities of the parties.

Any order which substantially affects the rights of the accused, or decide certain rights of the parties cannot be said to be an interlocutory order so as to bar a revision to the High Court against that order, because that would be against the very object which formed the basis.
for insertion or this particular provision in Section 397(2) of the 1973 Code.

Thus, for instance, orders summoning witnesses, adjourning cases, passing orders for bail, calling for reports and such other steps in aid of the pending proceedings, no doubt amount to interlocutory orders against which no revision would lie under Section 397(2) of the 1973 Code.

But orders which are matters of moment and which affect or adjudicate the rights of the accused or a particular aspect of the trial cannot be said to be interlocutory order so as to be outside the purview of the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court."
10.

The proposition laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court thus shows that the term interlocutory order used in the language of Section 397 (2) of Cr. P. C. has been used in a restricted sense and not in any broad or artistic sense.
Such an order merely denotes orders of a purely interim or temporary nature which do not decide or touch the important rights or liabilities of the parties.
Any order which substantially affects the rights of the parties or decide such rights, even if temporarily, cannot be claimed to be an interlocutory order so as to bar revision against such order.
The ratio in Ram Kishore Thakur, Directorate of Enforcement and Ganesha Murthy (supra) is on similar lines.

11. Perusal of order dated 01.07.2024 shows that the same authorizes respondent no.
2 to execute SPA with respect of sale of property situated at flat no. A-603, Ircon Apartment, Sector-18, Dwarka, Delhi.
The impugned order contains observations that the said property is of the accused and also observes that accused has every right to deal with his property as any other person.

The impugned order thus grants custody prole of six hours to the respondent no. 2 for executing the said SPA.
12.

Thus, the impugned order although granting custody prole to the accused affects substantial rights of the parties as well as the State by allowing the accused to execute SPA for sale of the said property, inasmuch as there are specific allegations in the charge-sheet that the said property had been purchased by respondent no. 2 from the funds siphoned off from the complainant society.
Furthermore, the premise of the said order is that the said property is of the accused.

However, the impugned order does not contain any observations as to if the said property was purchased by the Eminent Officers Welfare Society vs State And Ors on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49305278/
4 accused with money diverted/siphoned from the complainant society or from his own funds.

entities.text: Eminent Officers Welfare Society vs State And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. To my mind since substantial rights of the parties and the State are affected by the impugned order, the same cannot be said to be an interlocutory order.
Thus, the argument of respondent no. 2 in this regard is liable to be rejected.

14. Furthermore, as already observed when there are specific allegations in the charge-sheet that the said property was purchased with money diverted/siphoned from the funds of the complainant society, the observation that the property is of the accused and granting permission to respondent no. 2 to execute SPA with respect to sale of the said property would have the effect of disbelieving the prosecution version without trial.
15. It is argued on behalf of respondent no. 2 that the property in question was never attached.
In this context, clarifications were sought from the IO.

IO clarified that the original title documents were with concerned bank i.e. Central Bank of India (Central Bank Home Finance Ltd.) from which loan of Rs.49,00,000/- out of total sale consideration of Rs.1,71,00,000/- qua the property had been taken and necessary intimation was given to the concerned bank not to hand over original title documents to any person without permission of the court.
In Nevada Properties Pvt Ltd through its Director vs The State of Maharashtra AIR 2019 SC 4554 the Hon'ble Apex Court has enunciated the scope of powers of an I.O. under section 102 Cr.P.C.
It has been held that the investigating agency does not have any power to seize immoveable property although the title documents of the immoveable property can be seized.

16. Thus, in the facts of the present case, the IO could not have seized the property in question, however, notice was issued by the IO to the concerned bank having custody of the title documents not to release the original title documents without permission of the court.
Thus, merely because the property was never seized or attached is of no consequence for purposes of the present adjudication.
17. It was also argued on behalf of respondent no. 2 that the said property is not under dispute.

However, in face of specific allegations in the charge-sheet that the said property had been purchased from funds siphoned from the complainant/victim society, this argument is liable to be rejected at this stage.
18. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the present revision petition succeeds.
The impugned order dated 01.07.2024 is set aside.
Necessary intimation be sent to the Superintendent Jails.
It is clarified that nothing stated herein shall tantamount to expression of opinion on the merits of the case.

Counsel for the revisionist has already stated that under instructions from the revisionist, he was not pressing the reliefs seeking to restrain respondent no. 2 Eminent Officers Welfare Society vs State And Ors on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49305278/
5 Mukesh Kumar Singh and Neelam Singh from disposing off the said property and directions to respondent no. 2 Mukesh Kumar Singh to remit the sale proceeds of the said property.

sentences.text: Thus, nothing else survives for adjudication in the present matter.
20. Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
21. Trial Court Record be sent back along with copy of this order.
